regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 55.9","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY flatters. Triangulate: IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity confirm investment-led expansion, but core sector slipped to 4.8% YoY from 5.0% — the goods economy is not keeping pace with the headline. PMI Composite at 55.9 is services-heavy; decompose it and manufacturing at 55.1 is doing the real work, but new export orders bear watching. The quality of this growth is concentrated: capex is firing, consumption is coasting at 7.9% YoY passenger vehicle sales, and the informal economy — visible in two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY — is the one genuine surprise.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 5.54% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"CPI at 5.54% YoY, up from 3.21% two months ago, is the fastest two-month acceleration in this cycle. The decomposition is damning: food at 7.74% YoY and fuel at 22.93% YoY are doing the heavy lifting, but core CPI at 3.9% YoY means the RBI cannot dismiss this as transitory supply noise — demand is embedded. WPI at 9.92% YoY signals producer-price pressure that will feed into core CPI with a one-to-two quarter lag. Invert the consensus: if the RBI holds at 5.25% p.a. while CPI is printing above its 4% target and fuel inflation is at the 95th percentile, the real rate is compressing — not tightening — and the second-order effect is INR vulnerability.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.4% YoY; CD ratio 81%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.4% YoY against deposit growth at 17.8% YoY sounds like a narrowing gap — until you note that the 160 bps divergence has widened for two consecutive months and the CD ratio at 81% sits at the 71st percentile. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% during a rate-cut cycle was FY14; within twelve months, the taper tantrum forced an emergency reversal. Today's setup rhymes: NBFC credit accelerating at 15.8% YoY while corporate bond issuance collapses to ₹18,700 cr / month — the 4th percentile — signals wholesale funding markets are already rationing. The regulator's next move is macro-prudential, not rate-based.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate is eroding: CPI at 5.54% YoY puts the ex-post real rate near zero. The RBI's own inflation forecast of 5.1% YoY — revised up from 4.6% — implies the MPC knows the pause is uncomfortable. For housing, the average home loan rate at 7.35% p.a. is already 200 bps above repo; any further INR weakness that forces RBI's hand would reprice mortgages and compress affordability. The FX management calculus is the binding constraint: cutting into a 22.93% YoY fuel print with INR at the 89th percentile is not a policy the RBI can defend publicly.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY, rising from 16.1%, and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — up from 75.6% and now above the 75% threshold that historically triggers fresh private investment — together make the strongest case for a genuine capex upcycle since FY18. Iron ore at $161.91/t, up sharply from $92.71/t, confirms steel mill demand is real, not statistical. The inversion: core sector at 4.8% YoY, slipping from 5.0%, suggests infrastructure-linked output is not yet amplifying the manufacturing capex signal. Watch cement dispatches — absent from today's data but the critical triangulating proxy — before calling this a broad-based investment cycle.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹203521 cr/mo; PV 7.9% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,03,521 cr / month is a 74th-percentile print, but the prior month was ₹1,99,853 cr / month — the sequential acceleration is modest and partly reflects formalisation reclassifying existing spend, not new demand. Passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY are decelerating — down from 26.1% two months ago — while two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY are surging. That divergence is the signal: urban discretionary (PVs) is softening while rural mass-market (two-wheelers) is recovering, likely on the back of a better kharif season. Commercial vehicle sales at 12.6% YoY, falling for two consecutive months, suggest freight demand is not yet confirming the capex story.","badge_label":"Stable Consumption","badge_type":"b-neu"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.4% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence widening for 2 consecutive months (17.1%→19.4% credit; 9.9%→17.8% deposits). CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits, down from 82.2% but still elevated at 71st percentile. NBFC credit accelerating at 15.8% YoY (up from 10% YoY), now at 56th percentile. Corporate bond issuance at 18,700 ₹ cr / month — 4th percentile, signalling NBFCs and smaller banks are rationing retail deposits and turning to wholesale markets.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% and deposit franchises in metros (HDFC, Kotak, Axis). Underweight NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities — they face margin compression as deposit costs rise. RBI will likely cut rates in Q2 FY27 to ease deposit pressure, but only after inflation moderates. Position for 50-75 bps of cuts by September 2026.","pct_10y":71,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 71st percentile historically preceded either RBI rate cuts (2019-20) or aggressive NBFC deleveraging (2022-23). Current divergence is unsustainable; either deposits accelerate or credit growth moderates.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (latest), up from 16.1% YoY — 53rd percentile. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (latest), up from 75.6% — 68th percentile, now in the sweet spot for fresh capex. Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (down from 5% YoY) but still positive. Iron ore prices at $161.91 / t, up sharply from $92.71 / t (prev), signalling strong demand from steel mills and construction. Copper at $6.35 / lb, stable at 78th percentile.","implication":"Overweight capital goods manufacturers (Cummins, Timken, Rane Brake), cement (Ultratech, Ambuja), and steel (Tata Steel, JSW Steel). Capex cycle will sustain through FY27 as government infrastructure spending and private sector capacity additions run in parallel. Avoid consumer discretionary; capex is not yet translating to mass consumption.","pct_10y":68,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is historically the inflection point for fresh capex announcements. Last time this level was reached (2021-22), capex growth accelerated for 18 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit Record; Affluent Money Entering","data_text":"SIP inflows at 32,490 ₹ cr / month (latest), rising 3 consecutive months (29,845→31,961→32,297→32,490), now at 95th percentile. SIP accounts at 10.06 mn (latest), but SIP AUM at 17.86 ₹ lakh cr — implying average ticket size of ₹17.75 lakh per account, up from ₹16.8 lakh 2 months ago. Equity MF net inflows at 38,307 ₹ cr net / month (latest), up from 29,329 ₹ cr net / month, at 85th percentile. DII equity net at 51,829 ₹ cr net / month (96th percentile) vs FII equity net at -49,935 ₹ cr net / month (14th percentile).","implication":"SIP growth is real but skewed toward affluent retail (rising average ticket size). Expect SIP growth to decelerate in H2 FY27 as affluent money exhausts. Hedge with long-volatility positions; India VIX at 17.42 index (51st percentile) is complacent.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 95th percentile have historically preceded market corrections within 6-12 months (2021, 2023). Current affluent skew suggests retail euphoria is peaking.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI's Comfort Zone","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest), up from 20.05% YoY — 95th percentile, a strong-negative signal (score: -90). CPI headline at 5.54% YoY (latest), up from 4.83% YoY, rising 2 consecutive months (3.21%→4.45%→5.54%). Food inflation at 7.74% YoY (latest), up from 5.97% YoY, also rising 2 consecutive months. Brent crude at $91.72 / bbl (flat), WTI at $85.88 / bbl (flat), but FAO food index at 136 index (63rd percentile), up from 134.5 index. Natural gas at $3.21 / MMBtu (44th percentile).","implication":"RBI's inflation forecast of 5.1% YoY is at risk of being breached if fuel prices spike further (geopolitical risk) or food inflation persists. Avoid consumer staples with high fuel/logistics costs; margins will compress.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile last occurred in 2021-22 (oil shock post-Russia invasion). RBI held rates then; expect similar hawkishness now despite growth concerns.","is_surprise":false}

signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakness Accelerates; RBI Intervention Likely","data_text":"INR at 94.34 ₹ per USD (latest), up from 93.9 ₹ per USD — 89th percentile, a strong-negative signal (score: -78). FII equity net at -49,935 ₹ cr net / month (latest), a sharp reversal from +29,631 ₹ cr net / month 2 months ago (14th percentile). DII equity net at 51,829 ₹ cr net / month (96th percentile) is offsetting FII outflows but cannot sustain indefinitely. Gold in INR at 12,505 ₹ / g (latest), up from 12,447 ₹ / g — 100th percentile, signalling INR weakness and safe-haven demand. US 10Y Treasury yield at 4.86% yield (88th percentile) is attracting foreign capital away from India.","implication":"RBI will likely intervene to defend INR at 95 ₹ per USD level, using FX reserves. Position for INR to trade 94-96 ₹ per USD over next 3 months; avoid long INR bets.","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"INR at 89th percentile weakness last occurred in 2022-23 (Fed tightening cycle). RBI intervened then; expect similar action now. FII outflows are structural (higher US yields) and will persist.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Shift, Not IT Weakness","data_text":"Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (latest), down sharply from 19.5 mn sq ft / quarter 2 quarters ago — 0th percentile, a strong-negative signal (score: -100). Office vacancy at 13.4% vacant (latest), down from 14.5% vacant — improving despite low absorption. Nifty IT index flat while office rents in Bengaluru at 103.6 ₹ / sqft / mo (latest), down from 168.8 ₹ / sqft / mo 2 quarters ago. Retail mall vacancy at 11.15% vacant (latest), oscillating between 4.8% and 11.2% — highly volatile. Airline passenger traffic at 86.4 mn / month (latest), up from 85.17 mn / month — 32nd percentile, mild-negative signal (score: -36).","implication":"Office absorption collapse is NOT a sign of IT services weakness — it reflects a structural shift from traditional IT services to Global Capability Centers (GCCs) run by multinational corporates. GCCs occupy smaller, more flexible spaces (co-working, flex offices) that don't show up in traditional office absorption data. Traditional IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) are losing share to GCCs (Google, Microsoft, Amazon offices in Bangalore, Hyderabad). This is a 3-5 year secular headwind for IT services margins. Underweight large-cap IT services; overweight IT infrastructure plays (data centres, flex office operators like Awfis). Airline traffic at 32nd percentile suggests affluent travel is slowing — late-cycle signal.","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 0th percentile is unprecedented in the dataset. This is not cyclical; it's structural. GCC expansion is a permanent shift in India's services economy. What would prove this wrong: traditional IT services capex accelerates and office leasing rebounds within 2 quarters.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP, Zero Real Rate — Growth Quality Masks a Policy Trap

The facts:

  • GDP at 7.8% YoY is investment-led: IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity confirm the capex cycle is real.
  • But CPI at 5.54% YoY against repo at 5.25% p.a. leaves the ex-post real rate near zero — the RBI is effectively easing into an inflation overshoot.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY signal rural recovery; passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY — down from 26.1% two months ago — signal urban discretionary fatigue.
  • Core sector at 4.8% YoY, slipping from 5.0%, means infrastructure output is not yet amplifying the manufacturing investment signal.

The tension: The headline growth number and the capex data are genuine — but a near-zero real rate with fuel inflation at the 95th percentile means the RBI's pause is compressing the policy buffer, not preserving it.

Bottom line: Watch core CPI: if it breaches 4.5% YoY in the next print, the RBI's extended pause becomes indefensible and rate expectations will reprice sharply.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

Synchronised Tightening — Every Major Central Bank Still Hiking

The facts:

  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. — a 10-year high, 100th percentile — rising for three consecutive months; yen carry unwind is structural, not episodic.
  • Fed funds at 3.88% p.a. (75th percentile), rising three in a row; US 10Y Treasury at 4.86% yield (88th percentile) is doing additional tightening the Fed hasn't formally delivered.
  • US GDP SAAR at 3.4% SAAR, rising three consecutive quarters, gives the Fed no reason to pause — US PMI Composite at 58.4 (80th percentile) reinforces this.
  • But Eurozone CPI at 3.8% YoY with GDP at only 1.2% YoY shows the tightening cost is not evenly distributed — Europe is paying more for less.

The tension: US re-acceleration and BOJ normalisation are pulling global capital toward DM yields simultaneously — a combination that historically pressures EM currencies and equity flows within 60–90 days.

Bottom line: BOJ's next move is the underappreciated tail risk: a further 25 bps hike would accelerate yen carry unwind and test India's $680 bn reserve cushion directly.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Deposit Surge Masks Wholesale Funding Stress at the Margin

The facts:

  • Deposit growth at 17.8% YoY (87th percentile) looks healthy — but bank credit at 19.4% YoY means the 160 bps gap has widened for two consecutive months.
  • CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits (71st percentile) is easing from 83% but remains elevated; NBFC credit accelerating at 15.8% YoY adds a second funding demand layer.
  • But corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month — 4th percentile — signals NBFCs and smaller banks are being rationed out of wholesale markets.
  • SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (95th percentile) are channelling household savings into equities, not bank deposits — structurally tightening the deposit base.

The tension: Deposit growth looks adequate in aggregate, but the marginal funding stress is concentrated in NBFCs and smaller banks who cannot access bond markets at scale — the system is more fragile at the edges than the headline CD ratio implies.

Bottom line: Watch RBI's next macro-prudential circular: any increase in risk weights on NBFC lending would trigger a credit tightening faster than a rate hike.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Bank Nifty at 99th Percentile, REITs at Multi-Year Lows — Same Sector, Opposite Prices

The facts:

  • NRI buying is FALLING — NRI share of residential purchases at 18% (prior 15%, down 2 pp on the latest print); NRI share within premium/luxury at 32%; remittances at $144.8 bn (16% YoY) have not translated into property demand.
  • Hyderabad leads residential momentum: sales +15% YoY, launches +120% YoY, only 28 months unsold inventory — but NCR sales at -1% YoY and Chennai at -10% YoY show the recovery is city-specific.
  • Bank Nifty at 59,741 (99th percentile) is pricing a credit cycle with no funding stress — Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, Brookfield at ₹263/unit are all down 12–32% from prior prints.
  • Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (0th percentile) with GCCs at 42% of occupier mix — the REIT selloff is pricing IT services vacancy, not GCC demand.

The tension: Bank Nifty's 99th-percentile valuation assumes the credit cycle is clean; REIT prices at multi-year lows assume commercial real estate is impaired. Both cannot be right — and the CD ratio at 81% suggests the banks are the ones mispriced.

Bottom line: Avoid Bank Nifty at current levels; the REIT discount to NAV is more defensible if GCC absorption holds above 40% of the occupier mix.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — Inflation, Carry, and Credit

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile), rising from 20.05%, forces RBI's hand if CPI breaches 6% YoY — the probability × impact product is the highest on the board.
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) with US 10Y at 4.86% yield (88th percentile): yen carry unwind accelerates if BOJ hikes again — FII equity outflows at ₹49,935 cr net / month (14th percentile) are already the symptom.
  • CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits with corporate bond issuance at the 4th percentile: NBFC funding stress is the credit system's pressure valve — a macro-prudential tightening circular would transmit faster than any rate move.
  • But gold at ₹12,505/g (100th percentile) and INR at 94.34 ₹ (89th percentile) together signal the market is already hedging the inflation-currency feedback loop.

The tension: All three risks share a common detonator: a CPI print above 6% YoY would simultaneously force RBI off its pause, accelerate FII outflows, and expose NBFC funding gaps — the sequence is non-linear.

Bottom line: Watch the November CPI print: a reading above 6.0% YoY triggers the full cascade — rate repricing, INR pressure, and NBFC spread widening in the same fortnight.

"}
